text:
eli: heads-up — hitting a weird SSE resume/ordering bug in the onboarding sample. after an auth refresh i see fragments arrive out of order and a couple duplicates. repro by toggling offline for ~200ms during a ~900-token response.
eli: quick tcp-ish dump i grabbed:
```
[2026-12-08T10:04:12.100Z] conn open sid=onb-77
[2026-12-08T10:04:12.220Z] sse id=7 data=...
[2026-12-08T10:04:12.340Z] client reset (devtools)
[2026-12-08T10:04:12.580Z] reconnect resume=onb-77 last=7
[2026-12-08T10:04:12.720Z] sse id=9 data=...
[2026-12-08T10:04:12.830Z] sse id=8 data=...
[2026-12-08T10:04:12.920Z] sse id=9 data=... (duplicate)
```
eli: sample app uses fetch+reader (browser-sdk v0.9.7). code is naive append-on-read.
rachel: thanks. two quick q's: 1) does runtime emit an `id:` per logical fragment? 2) any local proxy in the chain?
eli: yes we emit `id:` for each chunk. local dev uses haproxy -> staging (not nginx). tcp capture shows server wrote the tail to two sockets in quick succession.
sam: probable cause: parallel reconnect+in-flight writes means server or proxy ends up sending overlapping data. haproxy's connection reuse/drain semantics may be relevant. client can also contribute by opening a new conn before the old is drained.
eli: i tried sending `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect and doing a small client-side LRU dedupe — that reduced duplicates but didn't fully fix reordering.
rachel: thoughts on SDK-level handling: instead of ad-hoc in sample apps, SDK could offer a streaming helper with: 1) persisted resume token and automatic Last-Event-ID on reconnect; 2) a fragment sequencer that accepts (id, payload) and emits in-order with a small reorder window (configurable ms) and a fallback flush; 3) idempotency filter (LRU or bloom) for duplicates; 4) jittered reconnect/backoff when auth refresh triggers repeated reconnects. expose as opt-in flag `stream-resume-mode: "lenient" | "ordered"`.
sam: +1. add telemetry hooks: emit events when out-of-order fragments or duplicates detected so infra/runtime can correlate with tcp captures. also make the sequencer pluggable so customers can choose strict vs best-effort reassembly.
eli: agree. i can prototype a small `fragmentSequencer` in sample-app and open a PR. also including a minimal repro harness that toggles network to mimic devtools.
rachel: infra follow-up: i'll open INFRA ticket to check haproxy drain settings and runtime emission guardrails (ensure we don't emit the same fragment to multiple sockets after resume). include the tcp capture and config.
sam: one more note: EventSource wrappers hide raw control of Last-Event-ID in some browsers; recommend SDK supports both fetch+reader and EventSource and normalizes resume semantics for both.
eli: good point. sample-app currently uses fetch path, but i'll add an EventSource demo and ensure SDK normalizes the header and id handling.
dev-bot: CI: sample-app-ci #934 passed (tests: 102) :white_check_mark:
eli: i'll open the PR with the sequencer prototype and link the infra ticket. tagging @rachel @sam for review. :thumbsup:
